name: Finerenone
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.dose: Start 10 mg (eGFR 25 to <60) or 20 mg (eGFR ≥60) once daily if K ≤5.0 mEq/L; target 20 mg once daily after 4 weeks
Start by eGFR as above; target 20 mg or 40 mg once daily

key_interactions.action: Monitor potassium when starting or changing either drug; adjust finerenone.

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Drugs or supplements that raise potassium

key_interactions.action: Monitor more often for their adverse reactions.

serious: Worsening kidney function in heart failure

monitoring: Serum potassium and eGFR before starting, at 4 weeks, after dose changes and periodically

pk.half_life_eskd: Not reported; no clinically relevant AUC change at eGFR 15 to <90 (label)
pk.metabolism: CYP3A4 (90%) and CYP2C8 (10%) to inactive metabolites
pk.excretion_renal_pct: About 80% in urine (under 1% unchanged); about 20% in feces
pk.dialyzability: Unlikely to be efficiently removed (about 90% protein bound; label).

sources.citation: Bayer HealthCare Pharmaceuticals Inc.. (2026). Kerendia (finerenone) [Prescribing information; US FDA-approved label, NDA215341, set ID fc726765-5d5a-4d6e-b037-b847bda9fb7c, version effective September 21, 2026]. DailyMed, U.S. National Library of Medicine.

draft_notes: Monitoring cadence ('at 4 weeks, after dose changes') follows label section 2.3; 'periodically' is our wording.
